dct_description_sm: Arctic aquatic systems are considered to be especially sensitive to anthropogenic disturbance, which can have cascading effects on the biological communities as aquatic food-web structure is altered. Bio-indicators that respond to major limnological changes, such as climate warming, can be used to detect and infer major environmental change with the use of paleolimnological techniques. A multi-proxy approach was used to quantify recent environmental changes at Baker Lake, Nunavut, Arctic Canada.
dct_title_s: A high resolution multi-proxy record of pronounced recent environmental change at Baker Lake, Nunavut
